account:
This morning I am in my office with the secretary and innkeeper. I have read both appointment books: office at 08:00, mill grain inspection at 10:00, lunch at home, council letters at 13:00, tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage at 15:00, office at 16:30, and the great hall lighting inspection at 18:00 before going home. The innkeeper has repeatedly confirmed the inspection and now offers to collect me from the office shortly beforehand. Eight lanterns have reportedly been installed around the hall tables.

There are several unusual loose ends. The town accounts ledger is missing. The secretary searched the hall tables and asked the builder, baker and innkeeper without locating it or receipts. We intend to review office storage and correspondence together. That is an unresolved administrative problem, not evidence by itself of wrongdoing.

Separately, the innkeeper collected bread from the baker and reportedly owes forty-four emeralds, payable after the jubilee. The order was described as private rather than a town expense. The secretary also reported that freight requested privacy about their arrangements until today at eighteen—the same time as my lighting inspection. Bread was found in one hall table. The repeated reminders, hall preparations, bread and timing make me suspect some gathering or jubilee-related celebration is being arranged, possibly as a surprise for me, with the inspection serving as the occasion to bring me there. That is only a suspicion: I have not seen a plan or established the order's original buyer or purpose.

Yesterday the neighbour repeated an unexplained rumour about a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' attributed to Townsfolk 02. Neither the neighbour nor I established any actual change. I cannot yet connect that rumour, the missing ledger, or the private freight arrangements with certainty. For now I should keep my appointments, review the office business, and distinguish what people have actually told me from my guesses.
